research.title: NCETM — Finding equivalent fractions and simplifying fractions
research.retrieval: Official HTML introduction and teaching points1–3. PriorB05 linkedPDF extraction/screenshot limitations remain; no full45-page visual-reading claim.
research.use: A common multiplicative relationship preserves fraction value; simplification divides both entries by a common factor.
research.ageAdaptation: English Year5 procedural scope narrowed: visual grouping first, divisibility vocabulary optional strong support, several legitimate paths accepted.
research.licence: NCETM default Crown/OGL exceptions; original prose/graphics only, no copied external media.

research.title: Oak National Academy — Use the relationship between the numerator and denominator to simplify fractions
research.retrieval: Official HTML learning points, keywords, misconception and teacher guidance plus licence. Embedded slides/video/worksheets not watched/read.
research.use: Use a visual part-whole or number-line representation to keep equivalence visible while numbers change.
research.ageAdaptation: Year5. Its highest-common-factor definition is not imposed as the only valid step: the frozen goal permits intermediate common-factor grouping.
research.licence: Page states OGLv3 except where otherwise stated; no text/figures/slides reused, third-party exceptions not presumed cleared.

research.title: Math Mammoth — Free fraction videos online, part2: Simplifying fractions
research.retrieval: Publisher-authored HTML description of simplifying section only; embedded10min video not watched.
research.use: Merging equal groups gives a visual interpretation of reduction; several small steps can replace one greatest-common-factor step.
research.ageAdaptation: Publisher places material with Grade5-B/Fractions2. Use only a bounded visual comparator, not imported curriculum scope or commercial efficacy claims.
research.licence: No open content-republication licence assumed. Link and conceptual comparison; no video, transcript, worksheets or pictures copied.

demoInventory.say: Kuusi kahdeksasosaa. Ryhmitellään palat kaksi kerrallaan: kahdeksasta palasta tulee neljä isoa palaa, ja väritetyistä kuudesta tulee kolme. Väliviivat häviävät, mutta väri pysyy paikallaan. Kuusi kahdeksasosaa on kolme neljäsosaa.

Kahdeksan kahdestoistaosaa: ensin jaetaan kahdella, saadaan neljä kuudesosaa. Vielä voi jakaa kahdella: kaksi kolmasosaa. Nyt ei enää löydy yhteistä jakajaa. Jos molemmista vain vähennettäisiin yksi, väri siirtyisi: se ei ole supistamista.
Kuusi yhdeksäsosaa: ryhmitellään kolme palaa kerrallaan, eli jaetaan kolmella. Saadaan kaksi kolmasosaa.

corrections: Three actual joinScene demos rather than stale one; reduce/place family explicitly inventoried.
Dividing both entries preserves value; no rule that merely reducing digits or subtracting one is simplification.
All positive integer common-factor paths accepted; partial4/6 from8/12 acknowledged as samevalue/validstep.
Equivalent but non-grouping answers are not described as unequal numbers; direct grouping restriction stated explicitly.
